structure.senior.tip: A bank loan for the purchase, repaid from the company's cash flow, secured and with covenants. The cheapest money and the first repaid.
structure.mezz.notes.tip: Bonds repaid after the senior loan. A high coupon, but no shares given away. The principal is repaid at maturity.
structure.mezz.convertible.tip: A low coupon; at exit the holders turn the bonds into shares. Nothing to repay, but our stake shrinks.
structure.mezz.notes.terms: Rate {rate} · principal repaid at maturity · no dilution
structure.mezz.convertible.terms: Rate {rate} · converts into {pct} of the shares at exit
structure.rollover.tip: The seller keeps part of the proceeds as shares in the new company. Our check is smaller, and the seller stays until the exit.
structure.rollover.terms: The seller keeps {pct} of the shares
structure.secondary.tip: Buying the shares the seller holds. The money goes to the seller; the company's cash does not change.
structure.secondary.terms: The part of the fund's check that goes to the seller
structure.primary.tip: The company issues new shares and the fund buys them. The money goes into the company for working capital or paying down debt. The fund's check grows by as much.
structure.primary.terms: Cash into the company, lowering net debt. Up to 30% of the price.
structure.lender.tip: Who lends the senior debt. A bank syndicate is cheap with tight covenants. A private credit fund costs more, lends more, sets looser covenants, and its money is committed, so sellers read the buyer as a sure closer.
structure.lender.bank.terms: Cheapest rate · leverage covenant 1.5x of headroom
structure.lender.private_credit.terms: Rate +{premium} · limit +{extra} · 2.5x of covenant headroom · sellers count it as certainty
structure.rate.tip: Floating moves with the policy rate every month. Fixed swaps today's rate at closing for the life of the loan. Fixed pays if rates rise; floating pays if they fall.
structure.rate.floating.terms: {rate} today · moves with the policy rate
structure.stake.tip: The share of the owner's existing shares the fund buys. Under half, so the owner keeps control.
structure.class.tip: Common shares split everything like the owner's. Preferred shares take back what went in first at an exit. Owners like preferred less.
structure.class.common.terms: Same terms as the owner · no downside protection
structure.class.preferred.terms: 1x liquidation preference · the owner is less likely to agree
